result.answer: Yes. A resend here would most likely have done harm. The failed message moves the patient to WARD-B, bed BAY2-04, at 08:20 UTC. The bed-management system has since applied a later transfer to WARD-C, bed BAY1-07, at 08:45 UTC (version 2). There is no receipt for the failed transfer. Resending it now would move the patient's recorded place back to a ward they have already left. Other systems take their information from that record. The bed board would show the wrong bed as taken and the WARD-C bed as free. Pharmacy would send medicines to WARD-B. Porters would get a task to move a patient who has already moved. Not acting does none of this, because the current record already matches the patient's latest known place. The one cost is that the short stay on WARD-B is missing from the movement history. Under W1, a site that keeps a full movement history would have sent this case to a person to decide. It would not have resent the message on its own. Shutter cannot see whether those other systems were ever affected, because they cannot be observed from here.

response.content: I've submitted my answer: yes, a resend would most likely have moved the patient's recorded place back to WARD-B after the later move to WARD-C, misleading the bed board, pharmacy and porters, and doing nothing avoids that.
